item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: six pieces of cardboard with length of the sides labeled in cm. Two of the pieces are square shaped with each side measured at 1 cm. Four of the pieces are rectangular shaped with two sides measured at 1 cm and two other sides measured at 2 cm.]

Susan has the 6 pieces of cardboard shown above. Which of the following shapes could Susan make using all 6 of these pieces without cutting them?
item.figure_description:
At the top of the item, six gray-shaded flat cardboard shapes are shown. Two are identical squares, each labeled '1 cm' on all four sides (top, bottom, left, and right). Four are identical horizontal rectangles, each labeled '2 cm' on the top and bottom sides and '1 cm' on the left and right sides.

The response options show line drawings of four 3D geometric solids with dashed lines representing hidden edges:
- Option A: A cube.
- Option B: A triangular prism resting on one of its rectangular faces.
- Option C: A truncated pyramid with a square or rectangular base and top.
- Option D: A tall right rectangular prism standing on a square base.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

C.

USE: 2 Trapezoid Tiles
MAKE: A 6-sided figure that is not the same shape as the one you made in Part B
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors: Any of four figures (6-sided) that was not used in part B.
Repeats a correct figure already given in part B
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part C response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Ariana found the following patterns to make containers. Which pattern actually makes the container shown beside it?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by squares and a cube to the right of the pattern]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by two circles on the ends of a rectangular shape and a cylinder to the right of the pattern]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by square and two triangles coming out of two sides of the square and a square base pyramid to the right of the pattern]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by two large rectangles and four small rectangles with two of the smaller rectangles coming out of the opposite shorter sides of the large rectangles and a rectangular prism]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four multiple-choice options, each showing a 2D net (with dashed interior fold lines) beside a 3D container (with dashed hidden edges):
- Option A: A net of 5 congruent squares arranged in an inverted U-shape (a row of 3 squares across the top, and 1 square hanging down from each of the left and right squares, leaving the middle space empty). Beside it is a line drawing of a cube.
- Option B: A net consisting of a horizontal rectangle with a circle attached to each of its two shorter vertical ends. Beside it is a line drawing of a vertical cylinder.
- Option C: A net consisting of a square with two triangles attached to adjacent sides: one extending down from the bottom side and one extending to the right from the right side. Beside it is a line drawing of an inverted square-based pyramid pointing downward.
- Option D: A net consisting of a horizontal row of four rectangles alternating in width (narrow, wide, narrow, wide), with a narrow rectangle attached to the top of the first wide rectangle and a narrow rectangle attached to the bottom of the second wide rectangle. Beside it is a line drawing of a matching upright rectangular prism.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A triangle on top of a rectangle]

The figure above is made from a rectangle and a triangle with three equal sides.
What is the length, in centimeters, of side AB ?
reference_items.figure_description: A composite figure composed of a rectangle at the bottom and a triangle on top sharing the rectangle's top edge as its base. The rectangle's bottom horizontal side is labeled "8 cm", and its right vertical side is labeled "3 cm". The triangle's top vertex is labeled A, and its bottom-right vertex (which is also the top-right corner of the rectangle) is labeled B.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: 3-D figure]

Which of these could be folded to make a shape like the 3-D figure above?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a perspective drawing of a right triangular prism lying horizontally on one rectangular face. The front and back faces are triangles, connected by three rectangular faces.

Below are four candidate nets labeled A, B, C, and D:
- A: A chain consisting of a rectangle at an angle, a triangle, a central horizontal rectangle, a triangle, and another rectangle angled upward.
- B: Three identical horizontal rectangles stacked vertically, with two triangles attached to the right edge of the top two rectangles, pointing to the right.
- C: Two horizontal rectangles stacked vertically with two triangles attached to their left side pointing left, and a third rectangle extending to the right with a triangle attached at its right end.
- D: Three identical horizontal rectangles stacked vertically in a column; one triangle is attached to the right side of the top rectangle pointing right, and another triangle is attached to the left side of the bottom rectangle pointing left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Here is a cone. Part of its surface is flat and part of its surface is curved.

[Image: A cone]

Which of these solids also has both a flat surface and a curved surface?
reference_items.figure_description: The figure in the stem is an upright circular cone resting on an elliptical-perspective circular base with a dashed rear edge. Option A shows a rectangular prism with all flat faces and dashed lines for interior/hidden edges. Option B shows a sphere with a dashed horizontal equator indicating curvature. Option C shows a triangular pyramid (tetrahedron) with flat triangular faces and dashed lines for hidden base edges. Option D shows a right circular cylinder standing upright, with a flat circular top, a flat circular bottom (with a dashed rear edge), and a curved lateral side.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
A square grid containing six outlined shapes labeled A through F:
- Shape A: A square measuring 3 units by 3 units.
- Shape B: An irregular stepped polygon with horizontal and vertical edges of varying lengths (not 4 sides, sides of different lengths).
- Shape C: A vertical rectangle measuring 2 units wide and 5 units tall.
- Shape D: A symmetrical 12-sided cross (plus sign) shape composed of five 2-by-2 square sections; every side is 2 units long.
- Shape E: An isosceles trapezoid with a horizontal top base of 4 units, a horizontal bottom base of 6 units, and a height of 4 units.
- Shape F: A square oriented as a rhombus/diamond with horizontal and vertical diagonals measuring 4 units; all 4 sides are of equal length.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Three arrangements of 3 tiles labeled Rita, Ina, and Lana]

Rita, Ina, and Lana take turns arranging 3 tiles. Each arranges the tiles in a different shape as shown above. Which of the following is true about the area of the shapes?

options.label: A
options.text: Rita’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: B
options.text: Ina’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: C
options.text: Lana’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: D
options.text: All of the shapes have the same area.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three arrangements of three tiles each, labeled "Rita", "Ina", and "Lana":
- Rita: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. A triangle sits on top of the left square, with its base along the top edge of that square and its apex pointing upward.
- Ina: A square sits at the top with horizontal top and bottom edges. Attached below it is a triangle sharing the square's bottom horizontal edge and pointing downward. Attached to the lower-right edge of the triangle is a second square, tilted diagonally downward and to the right.
- Lana: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. Attached to the right vertical edge of the right square is a triangle pointing to the right.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
